common_name: Southern Comfort Heuchera (Heat-Tolerant Peach Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; the villosa parentage gives Southern Comfort excellent heat and humidity tolerance, making it one of the more reliable heucheras for zone 9 Gulf South gardens.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Southern Comfort is a large, vigorous Heuchera villosa selection bred by Dan Heims of Terra Nova Nurseries specifically to bring Heuchera's colorful foliage to hot, humid climates where hosta-and-heuchera-border classics from cooler regions often struggle. The huge, ruffled leaves emerge peach-apricot and mature to a warm cinnamon-caramel, holding their color and substance through Gulf South summer heat far better than most Heuchera americana hybrids. Airy sprays of small white flowers rise well above the foliage in summer. Because it is one of the most heat- and humidity-tolerant heucheras available, Southern Comfort is a strong first choice for zone 9 gardeners who have struggled to keep other coral bells alive through a Gulf Coast summer. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in early spring.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Perennials for Shade

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; morning sun deepens the peach-pink color of the ruffled leaves.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade with some protection from intense afternoon sun; Georgia Peach is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with large, heavily ruffled leaves that open peachy-orange and shift toward soft rose-pink as they mature, giving the clump a shifting, multi-toned color display through the season. The undersides of the leaves show a deep purple-red that peeks through as the ruffled margins curl, adding extra depth to the foliage color. Small cream-white flowers appear on wiry stems in late spring above the foliage mound. Give it sharp drainage and consistent soil moisture, since this heuchera dislikes both waterlogged crowns and prolonged drought. Divide congested clumps in early spring every 3-4 years to keep the planting vigorous and well-shaped.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens
